blocks.text: The leaders of the four-nation Quad grouping agreed Tuesday to deepen cooperation on maritime monitoring, artificial intelligence and cybersecurity, steadily expanding areas of cooperation across administrations amid China’s growing military and economic influence in the Indo-Pacific. In a joint press release issued after a summit in Manila — their first in more than two years — the leaders of Australia, India, Japan and the United States said they would conduct their first maritime surveillance training flights in the Pacific next year and enhance cybersecurity cooperation in the Indo-Pacific region.
